title: Organic mechanisms: whole mechanisms and focused marking groups
authorship: Original practice questions informed by four questions in user-supplied OCR Chemistry A H432/02 papers. Not OCR-authored questions or official mark schemes.
delivery: Standalone drawing practice with teacher/self marking. Not imported into questions.json; not automatically scored by the revision tool.
assessment: Full-headed curly arrows represent movement of an electron pair. Draw their tails at the electron source and their heads at the destination. Show formal and partial charges distinctly. A mark group containing several requirements earns one mark only when all requirements are met; no half marks. The focused questions repeat the same groups as the combined questions and do not constitute additional independent coverage.
sourceVerification: Read from the six user-uploaded PDFs, including rendered scheme diagrams. Web access was blocked; official download URLs inferred from filenames have not been independently checked. Page references below distinguish printed pages from one-based PDF pages.

sources.session: 2020 autumn: paper dated 13 October; scheme labelled November
sources.question: 19(c)(i)
sources.sourceReaction: HCN addition to the supplied branched aldehyde F.
sourceCaveats: Carbonyl dipole and C=O-to-O arrow earn one mark together.
The protonation mark requires the correct alkoxide intermediate as well as the arrow.
Cyanide attacks through carbon. The arrow can start at its carbon lone pair or the negative charge on carbon.

For protonation, attack on H+ or on a hydrogen of water is allowed. The source ignores an attempted water O-H bond-breaking arrow and a missing water dipole. A complete water pathway is shown in the original answer guidance.

sources.question: 16(b)(i)
sources.sourceReaction: HBr addition to but-1-ene, showing the major-product mechanism.
sourceCaveats: H-Br dipole and H-Br bond-breaking arrow earn one mark together.
The correct carbocation and Br− attack arrow earn one mark together; δ+ does not replace a formal + charge.
The source explicitly allows error carried forward for a product from an incorrect carbocation. This needs human judgement; do not silently replace it with exact-answer-only exam marking.
Do not place a partial charge on the starting C=C bond. The source refers use of Br2 instead of HBr to a team leader.

sources.question: 16(a)(ii)
sources.sourceReaction: Br2 addition to 3-methylhex-2-ene, not to but-2-ene.
sourceCaveats: The induced Br-Br dipole and BOTH first-stage arrows earn ONE mark together.
The correct carbocation consistent with the mechanism and Br− attack earn one mark together. Either original alkene carbon can carry the positive charge in the source.
The third mark is for the product matching the mechanism; its guidance continues onto printed page 12 (PDF page 13). Do not import an identical explicit carbocation ECF rule from the 2021 scheme.

A bromonium route is allowed with team-leader referral in the source. The original exercises deliberately specify the open-chain carbocation representation; a bromonium mechanism must not be presented as chemically wrong.

The source disallows HBr in place of Br2 but allows ECF for subsequent use. It disallows partial charge on C=C. Its arrow guidance includes examiner-specific ECF; the draft is not a replica of those examiner procedures.

sources.question: 20(a)(iii)
sources.sourceReaction: Chlorination of substituted benzene J, including the halogen carrier's role.
sourceCaveats: Electrophile generation AND catalyst regeneration earn ONE mark together, not one mark per equation.
The remaining marks are π-system attack, correct arenium ion, and C-H-to-ring arrow respectively.
AlCl3, FeCl3 and other suitable halogen carriers are allowed by the source. The original question supplies AlCl3, and the focused question explicitly permits a consistent FeCl3 alternative.
The partial π-ring must extend over more than half the hexagon with its gap facing the attacked carbon; the positive sign may be anywhere inside the hexagon.
Source-specific positional guidance for substituted J is not transferred to the benzene analogue. The new item does not assess directing effects or regioselectivity.

families.title: HCN addition to methanal
families.transferNote: Methanal replaces the source's branched aldehyde. It preserves the five marking groups while avoiding stereochemical and alkyl-chain distractions.
families.combinedPrompt: Methanal, H2C=O, reacts with HCN in the presence of cyanide ions. Draw the complete mechanism, showing curly arrows, relevant dipoles and charges, the intermediate and the organic product. Name the mechanism. You may show protonation using H+ or water.
families.diagramBrief: Draw methanal with its C=O bond clear and show a separate cyanide ion with unambiguous carbon and nitrogen labels. The student view must not pre-fill the carbonyl dipole, attack arrow, intermediate or product. Provide separate, uncrossed drawing areas for attack and protonation.

groups.label: Cyanide attack
groups.sourceAward: Arrow from cyanide's carbon electron pair/negative charge to the carbonyl carbon.
groups.prompt: Draw methanal and CN−. Add the curly arrow showing where cyanide donates its electron pair to the carbonyl group. Make the attacking end of cyanide unambiguous.
requirements: Cyanide attacks through carbon, not nitrogen.
The full-headed arrow starts at the carbon lone pair or negative charge on carbon and ends at the carbonyl carbon.
groups.modelAnswer: An arrow from the carbon lone pair/negative charge of −C≡N to C of H2C=O.
commonErrors: Starting the arrow at nitrogen.
Starting at the carbonyl carbon and pointing to cyanide.
Pointing cyanide at oxygen.
groups.feedback: Cyanide donates through carbon to the electron-deficient carbonyl carbon.

groups.label: Carbonyl polarity and bond opening
groups.sourceAward: Correct carbonyl dipole AND C=O-to-O arrow together.
groups.prompt: On methanal, show the relevant carbonyl dipole and the curly arrow for movement of the C=O π electrons during nucleophilic addition. Both are needed for the mark.
requirements: Carbonyl carbon is δ+ and oxygen is δ−.
A full-headed curly arrow goes from the C=O bond to oxygen.
groups.modelAnswer: H2Cδ+=Oδ− with an arrow from the C=O bond to O.
commonErrors: Correct arrow but missing or reversed dipole.
Arrow from O into the C=O bond.
Formal +/− charges used on the neutral starting carbonyl in place of δ+/δ−.
groups.feedback: The π pair moves to oxygen. Show the starting dipole as well; this is one combined mark.

groups.label: Intermediate and protonation
groups.sourceAward: Correct alkoxide intermediate AND O-to-proton arrow together.
groups.prompt: After CN− adds to methanal, draw the intermediate and show its protonation using H+ or water. Show the charge and the electron-pair source clearly.
requirements: Correct alkoxide intermediate: −O–CH2–C≡N, with a single C–O bond and negative charge on O.
A full-headed arrow starts at the O lone pair or O− charge and ends at H+ or a hydrogen of water.
groups.modelAnswer: −O–CH2–C≡N; arrow from O− to H+. Alternatively, arrow from its O lone pair to H of H2O; a complete water pathway also shows that water O–H bond's electrons returning to water O, producing OH−.
commonErrors: Correct protonation arrow drawn on an incorrect intermediate.
Oδ− substituted for the intermediate's formal O− charge.
Arrow from H+ towards oxygen.
Cyanide bonded through nitrogen.
groups.feedback: The intermediate is an alkoxide. Its negatively charged oxygen donates a pair to a proton.

groups.label: Hydroxynitrile product
groups.prompt: Draw the organic product when methanal reacts with HCN. Show connectivity clearly; a molecular formula alone is insufficient.
requirements: HO–CH2–C≡N, with the new C–C bond and OH on the former carbonyl carbon.
groups.modelAnswer: HO–CH2–C≡N (2-hydroxyethanenitrile). A correct unambiguous structure is sufficient; its name is not an extra requirement.
commonErrors: An N-bonded isocyanide product.
Leaving a C=O bond in the addition product.
Omitting the OH group or the added carbon.
groups.feedback: Addition forms a hydroxynitrile and adds one carbon to the original carbonyl skeleton.

groups.label: Mechanism name
groups.prompt: Name the mechanism when HCN reacts with methanal in the presence of cyanide ions.
requirements: Nucleophilic addition.
commonErrors: Nucleophilic substitution.
Electrophilic addition.
groups.feedback: CN− is a nucleophile and adds across the carbonyl; no group is substituted.

families.title: HBr addition to 2-methylpropene
families.transferNote: 2-Methylpropene replaces but-1-ene. The intended route forms a tertiary rather than secondary carbocation; this changes the substrate without changing the four assessed groups. This is ordinary electrophilic addition, not peroxide-initiated radical addition.
families.combinedPrompt: 2-Methylpropene, CH2=C(CH3)2, reacts with hydrogen bromide by electrophilic addition. Draw the mechanism for the major product. Include curly arrows, the H–Br dipole, the charged intermediate and the organic product.
families.diagramBrief: Show CH2=C(CH3)2 with the double bond unobstructed, and separate H–Br. Leave the dipole and all arrows blank. Keep the subsequent carbocation and nucleophile in a separate stage with room for a clear Br−-to-carbon arrow.

groups.label: Alkene attack on H
groups.prompt: Show the first curly arrow when 2-methylpropene reacts with HBr. Draw enough of both reactants to identify the electron source and destination.
requirements: A full-headed arrow starts at the C=C bond and ends at H of H–Br.
Do not add a partial charge to the starting C=C bond.
groups.modelAnswer: Arrow from the C=C π bond to H of H–Br.
commonErrors: Arrow from H to C=C.
Arrow to Br rather than H.
Starting at one carbon atom instead of the electron pair in the bond.
groups.feedback: The alkene π pair is the electron source; hydrogen is the electrophilic destination.

groups.label: HBr polarity and bond breaking
groups.sourceAward: Correct H–Br dipole AND bond-breaking arrow together.
groups.prompt: Show the dipole on HBr and its bond-breaking curly arrow during addition to an alkene. Both are needed for the mark.
requirements: Hδ+–Brδ−.
A full-headed arrow from the H–Br bond to Br.
groups.modelAnswer: Hδ+–Brδ−, with the bond electron pair moving to Br to form Br−.
commonErrors: Correct dipole without the arrow.
Reversed dipole.
Arrow to H, producing H−.
groups.feedback: Br takes the H–Br bond pair. The dipole and arrow form one marking group.

groups.label: Major-route carbocation and Br− attack
groups.sourceAward: Correct carbocation AND Br−-to-C+ arrow together.
groups.prompt: For the major-product route of HBr addition to 2-methylpropene, draw the carbocation intermediate and the curly arrow for its reaction with Br−.
requirements: The tertiary carbocation (CH3)3C+ is drawn with a formal + charge at the central carbon.
A full-headed arrow starts at a Br− lone pair or its negative charge and ends at that C+.
groups.modelAnswer: (CH3)3C+ plus Br−; arrow from a Br− electron pair/negative charge to the positively charged central carbon.
commonErrors: Primary (CH3)2CH–CH2+ used for the major-product route.
δ+ instead of + on the carbocation.
Arrow from C+ to Br−.
Correct arrow drawn on an incorrect intermediate.
groups.feedback: The major route forms the more stable tertiary carbocation. Bromide donates the pair that makes the new C–Br bond.

groups.label: Major organic product
groups.sourceAward: Correct product; source permits ECF from an incorrect carbocation.
groups.prompt: Draw the major organic product from electrophilic addition of HBr to 2-methylpropene. Show connectivity clearly.
requirements: (CH3)3C–Br, 2-bromo-2-methylpropane.
commonErrors: 1-Bromo-2-methylpropane given as the major product.
A dibromoalkane, as though the reagent were Br2.
groups.feedback: Br is bonded to the carbon that carried the positive charge in the major-route intermediate.
groups.combinedMarkingNote: For the combined drawing task, a teacher may award this product group by error carried forward if the student drew the other carbocation and the product follows correctly from it. M3 is still lost for the wrong major-route intermediate. In this independent focused task no earlier intermediate is supplied, so require the stated major product.

families.title: Bromine addition to ethene
families.transferNote: Ethene replaces 3-methylhex-2-ene. It preserves the three marking groups but removes regioisomer and stereochemistry choices. Use the specified open-chain carbocation representation. Bromonium mechanisms are chemically valid and are accepted with referral in the original scheme; they are not distractors here.
families.combinedPrompt: Ethene reacts with bromine. Using the open-chain carbocation representation for this exercise, draw the electrophilic addition mechanism. Include the induced dipole on Br2, all electron-pair arrows, the charged intermediate and the organic product.
families.diagramBrief: Show ethene and a separate Br–Br bond, with neither a dipole nor any arrows pre-filled. Allow either orientation of the induced dipole when the arrow destinations agree. Draw the intermediate in a separate area. Do not place δ charges on ethene.

groups.label: Induced dipole and two first-stage arrows
groups.sourceAward: Br–Br dipole AND C=C-to-Brδ+ arrow AND Br–Br bond-breaking arrow together: ONE mark.
groups.prompt: Show the first stage when ethene reacts with Br2. Include the induced dipole on Br–Br and both curly arrows for formation of the carbon–bromine bond and breaking of Br–Br. All three features are needed for the mark.
requirements: A correctly oriented Brδ+–Brδ− induced dipole.
A full-headed arrow from the C=C bond to the Brδ+ atom.
A full-headed arrow from the Br–Br bond to Brδ−.
Do not put a partial charge on the starting C=C bond.
groups.modelAnswer: Brδ+–Brδ−: C=C → Brδ+ and Br–Br bond → Brδ−. A left/right mirror orientation is equally valid if all labels and arrows remain consistent.
commonErrors: Only one of the two arrows shown.
Both arrows correct but dipole missing.
Arrow to Brδ− from the alkene.
Treating this group as three marks.
groups.feedback: The alkene polarises bromine. The dipole and both first-stage arrows together earn one mark.

groups.label: Intermediate and bromide attack
groups.sourceAward: Correct carbocation matching mechanism AND Br−-to-C+ arrow together.
groups.prompt: Using the open-chain carbocation representation, draw the intermediate after ethene reacts with Br2 and show its reaction with Br− using a curly arrow.
requirements: BrCH2–CH2+ (or the reflected equivalent), with one attached Br and one formally positive carbon.
A full-headed arrow from a Br− lone pair/negative charge to C+.
groups.modelAnswer: BrCH2–CH2+ plus Br−; arrow from Br− to the positive carbon. The reflected intermediate +CH2–CH2Br is equivalent.
commonErrors: No attached Br on the intermediate.
δ+ instead of a formal + charge.
Arrow drawn from carbon to bromide.
groups.feedback: The first Br is already bonded. The second Br comes from bromide donating an electron pair to the carbocation.

groups.label: Dibromoalkane product
groups.prompt: Draw the organic product from addition of Br2 to ethene. Show the location of both Br atoms.
requirements: BrCH2–CH2Br: 1,2-dibromoethane.
groups.modelAnswer: BrCH2–CH2Br, with one Br on each former alkene carbon.
commonErrors: Bromoethane, as though the reagent were HBr.
Both Br atoms placed on the same carbon.
Leaving the C=C bond in the product.
groups.feedback: The double bond is replaced by a C–C single bond and one C–Br bond at each carbon.

families.title: Catalysed chlorination of benzene
families.reaction: C6H6 + Cl2 → C6H5Cl + HCl; AlCl3 catalyst
families.transferNote: Benzene replaces substituted arene J. The four marking groups are retained, but substituent-directed positions and side-chain chemistry are not assessed. Use the partial-circle arenium-ion convention to match this scheme.
families.combinedPrompt: Benzene reacts with Cl2 in the presence of anhydrous AlCl3. Draw the electrophilic substitution mechanism, including the intermediate, charges and curly arrows. Give equations showing formation of the electrophile and regeneration of the catalyst. Show the organic product.
families.diagramBrief: Use a large benzene hexagon and inner circle. Place the electrophile away from any ring labels. Leave a separate intermediate area with room to show H and Cl on the same carbon, the partial π-ring, positive charge and C–H arrow without crossing labels. Product is required for a complete response but is not an extra fifth mark.

groups.label: Electrophile generation and catalyst regeneration
groups.sourceAward: BOTH catalyst equations together: ONE mark.
groups.prompt: Write two equations for chlorination of benzene: one forming the electrophile from Cl2 and AlCl3, and one regenerating AlCl3. Both are needed for the mark. You may instead use FeCl3 consistently in both equations.
requirements: Cl2 + AlCl3 → Cl+ + AlCl4−.
H+ + AlCl4− → AlCl3 + HCl.
Alternatively, both corresponding FeCl3/FeCl4− equations are correct. Do not mix aluminium and iron species between the pair.
groups.modelAnswer: Cl2 + AlCl3 → Cl+ + AlCl4−; H+ + AlCl4− → AlCl3 + HCl. Alternative pair: Cl2 + FeCl3 → Cl+ + FeCl4−; H+ + FeCl4− → FeCl3 + HCl.
commonErrors: Giving only electrophile formation.
Cl− instead of Cl+.
Not regenerating the catalyst.
Treating the two equations as two marks.
groups.feedback: The halogen carrier generates the electrophile and is regenerated. Both equations together earn one mark.

groups.label: π-system attack
groups.sourceAward: Arrow from arene π-system to Cl+.
groups.prompt: Draw benzene and Cl+. Add the curly arrow showing formation of the carbon–chlorine bond during electrophilic attack.
requirements: A full-headed arrow starts at the benzene π-system and ends at Cl+.
groups.modelAnswer: Curly arrow from the inner π-circle to Cl+.
commonErrors: Arrow from Cl+ to the ring.
Arrow from a C–H bond.
Cl− used as the attacking species.
groups.feedback: The arene π electrons donate to the electrophile; the positive chlorine is the destination, not the source.

groups.label: Arenium-ion intermediate
groups.sourceAward: Correct intermediate, partial π-ring and formal positive charge.
groups.prompt: Draw the arenium-ion intermediate immediately after benzene attacks Cl+. Use the partial-circle convention, showing the attached H and Cl, the remaining delocalisation and the charge.
requirements: H and Cl are attached to the same, attacked ring carbon.
The inner partial π-ring extends over more than half the hexagon, with its gap facing that carbon.
A formal + sign appears inside the ring; a full aromatic circle is absent.
groups.modelAnswer: A six-membered ring with H and Cl on the attacked carbon, an inner partial circle extending over more than half the ring with a gap towards that carbon, and + inside the hexagon.
commonErrors: A complete aromatic circle retained after addition.
Missing + or using δ+.
A partial-circle gap facing the wrong carbon.
Removing H before drawing the intermediate.
groups.feedback: Attack temporarily breaks aromaticity. The attacked carbon retains H and gains Cl; the positive charge is delocalised over the remaining π-system.

groups.label: Restoring the aromatic ring
groups.prompt: Starting from the arenium ion in benzene chlorination, show the curly arrow for restoration of aromaticity. Make the tail and head unambiguous and show the resulting organic product.
requirements: A full-headed arrow starts at the C–H bond on the carbon bearing Cl and ends inside the ring to restore the π-system.
groups.modelAnswer: Curly arrow from the C–H bond at the Cl-bearing carbon into the ring. H+ is lost and chlorobenzene forms. Product is shown for completeness, with no extra mark allocated.
commonErrors: Arrow beginning on H rather than the C–H bond.
Arrow taking the C–Cl bond pair back into the ring.
Arrow from the ring towards H.
groups.feedback: The C–H bond pair returns to the π-system as H+ is lost; the C–Cl bond remains.

toolIntegrationNotes: Content draft only. Do not concatenate this file into questions.json: its schema is deliberately separate and it is not a ready-to-import bank migration.

Suggested future bank mapping: mechanism-completion with essential components, one per mark group, each worth one mark. Four combined cards require 5, 4, 3 and 4 components; sixteen focused cards require one each.

The current arrow-only score cannot assess correct dipoles, intermediates, products or equation pairs. Full drawing answers in this pack need teacher/self marking. A future automatically marked adaptation can use whole-diagram choices or structured components, clearly labelled recognition practice.

For recognition items, each answer option for a grouped mark must contain all its requirements, or all its subcomponents must be correct before the single point is awarded. Do not allocate separate points to each arrow, dipole or equation.
Recognition scores are not equivalent to freely drawing mechanisms. Do not claim exact OCR examiner scoring, error-carried-forward judgement or full mechanism production from selected answers.

A combined recognition card must not reveal the answers to other parts through its intermediate, dipole or model-arrow diagrams. Show model answers only after submission/reveal; record reveal/retry attempts separately from first unaided performance.

Use the existing site font, line weights, palette and question feedback structure for future assets. All new diagrams should be original, not crops of the uploaded papers. Prefer separate stage panels with short, uncrossed leader lines and responsive layouts.

An asterisk or other electron-source cue belongs in an explicitly supported learning mode. It gives away a source-identification answer and must not appear in an unaided assessment of the arrow source.

No student answers, identities or account data are stored by the standalone preview. It has no external scripts, network requests, analytics or persistence. No Supabase changes are needed to review this draft.

Before bank integration: chemistry teacher review, original SVG production, answer-leakage/accessibility checks, scoring/coverage tests, a new bank version and a NEW additive catalogue migration. Never rewrite an already-applied migration. Keep current student/browser progress compatible.
